exam_scheme.note: The Joint Entrance Screening Test (JEST) is conducted nationwide by a consortium of premier Indian autonomous research institutes (including BARC, Bose Institute, HRI, ICTS, IGCAR, IIA, IISc, IISERs, IMSc, IOP, IPR, IUCAA, JNCASR, NCRA-TIFR, NISER, PRL, RRCAT, RRI, SINP, SNBNCBS, TIFR, and VECC) for screening candidates seeking admission to Ph.D. and Integrated M.Sc.-Ph.D. programmes in Physics, Theoretical Computer Science, Neuroscience, and Computational Biology. JEST is recognized as a National Eligibility Test (NET) by SERB. The Physics examination is a 3-hour test carrying 100 marks across 50 questions divided into three parts: Part A (15 multiple-choice questions, +3 marks for correct, -1 mark for wrong), Part B (10 integer/numerical questions, +3 marks for correct, no negative marking), and Part C (25 multiple-choice questions, +1 mark for correct, -1/3 mark for wrong). Each participating institute calls candidates for independent personal interviews based on JEST percentile ranks.
